Article Title: Winter is coming: From capacity to safety, the things you cannot miss in your next Geyser
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

Start with the right capacity

Storage or instant?

Check the energy rating

Tank material and hard water

Pressure rating matters

Installation is part of safety

Smart features and after-sales service

Before you buy

As temperatures begin to dip across the country, the geyser moves from an afterthought to a daily essential. Few things feel worse than stepping into a cold bathroom on a frosty morning only to find the water barely lukewarm, and few household appliances are as easily taken for granted until they fail. Whether you are replacing an ageing unit that has served you for a decade or buying your first, the choices you make now will shape your winter in more ways than one. The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. On the other hand, a hasty and uninformed purchase would mean weeks of cold showers, repeated repairs and in worse cases can also lead to some accident. So, from capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy, so your geyser keeps you warm without nasty surprises.The first thing to check while buying a geyser is the capacity. Always keep in mind that bigger is not always better. A larger tank takes a lot of time to heat and it also uses more amount of electricity. So, it’s important that you decide of the capacity of the geyser with the size of your family.* 1 to 3 people: A 15-litre geyser is usually enough.* 4 to 5 people: Look at 25 litres.* Larger households or multiple bathrooms: Go for 35 litres or more, or consider more than one unit.* Kitchen or washbasin use: A 3 to 6-litre instant geyser heats water in seconds and suits small, quick needs.If your family showers at the same time every morning, size up. If usage is spread through the day, a smaller tank works.Another important parameter to keep in mind while purchasing a geyser is whether to go for storage or instant model. The Storage geyser heats the water in a tank and keeps it hot. This functionality of storage geyser makes it a better option for bathrooms and several users. On the other hand, instant geysers heat water as it flows, so there is no waiting and no standby loss, but the flow will also be limited. On the other hand, gas geysers are also an option where piped gas is available, however, they need an excellent source of ventilation, as poor airflow can cause buildup of carbon monoxide. It is advisable to never install gas geyser in closed bathrooms.It is always important to check the energy star rating before buying any electrical appliance. Buyers should keep in mind that a geyser may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters a lot. Always look for Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) star rating. Remember that a 5-star unit uses less standby energy as compared to a poorly rated one. The device with 5-star rating will come with a heftier price tag but it will eventually help you a lot in saving your electricity cost later. Good insulation, usually polyurethane foam around the tank, keeps water hot for longer and reduces how often the heater switches on.The inner tank decides how long the geyser lasts. Stainless steel tanks resist corrosion well, while glass-lined or coated tanks offer a cheaper alternative. If your area has hard water, as many parts of north India do, scale will build up on the heating element and shorten its life. Look for a geyser with a corrosion-resistant tank and a magnesium anode, and plan to descale it once a year.Not all geysers can handle all plumbing. If you live in a high-rise or use a pressure pump, check the working pressure the geyser is built for. Buying a unit rated for lower pressure than your supply can cause leaks or even tank damage.Safety features you should not skipThis is where it pays not to cut corners.* ISI mark: Always ensure that the geyser carries an ISI mark rating which clearly states that the device meets Indian safety standards.* Thermostat and thermal cut-out: These markers stop the geyser when water reaches the set temperature, and then cut off power if it overheats.* Pressure relief or safety valve: The safety valve reduced the excess pressure and decreases the risk of tank bursting.* Water-protection rating: Always look for IPX4 or higher rating as it protects the geyser from splashes in damp bathrooms.* Earthing and ELCB: Always use a three-pin plug with proper earthing, and consider an ELCB or RCCB on the circuit to guard against electric shock.Geysers draw a lot of current, so use a dedicated switch and wiring rated for the load. Avoid plugging them into a loose or overloaded socket.A filled 25-litre geyser can weigh well over 30 kg. It should be fixed to a strong wall with the brackets supplied, not mounted on a weak partition. Install it out of direct splash, ideally outside the shower area, and use only an authorised technician. Make sure the inlet and outlet pipes are fitted correctly and that the safety valve is not blocked.Nowadays, a lot of models are available in the market which comes with various smart features. For instance, the geysers now come with timers, digital temperature displays and app control which can help reduce the use of power and also prevent the appliance from staying on the entire day. These features are use but they should not come at a cost of other important safety features. Also, always check for the warranty, which usually covers the tank fr longer than the heating element. Also, make sure that you go for a brand which has a proper service network in your city.Before buying your new geyser it is important that you compare the capacity, star rating, tank material, safety features and warranty rather than only the price. A well and thoughtfully selected geyser would last for years and also a care purchase made now will payoff in the upcoming and every other winter morning.
Article Summary: The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. From capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy. Buyers should keep in mind that a geysers may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters.

Article Title: Fake Google Chrome app with over 1 lakh downloads found on Google Play: How to spot and what to do next
Article Text:
Google Play

Fake Google Chrome app hiding in plain sight as an ad

From a casual game to a fake browser

How to spot fake apps and avoid scams

Check the publisher directly underneath the app title to ensure it matches the official creator or parent company.

Paid ad placements only mean someone paid for visibility; they do not guarantee legitimacy.

High install tallies do not automatically confirm safety, especially if an older app has been repurposed.

Be alert to installed apps that unexpectedly change their identity, icon, or functionality.

What to do if you installed the app

A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store , displaying over 1 lakh (100,000) downloads and securing a paid “sponsored” placement directly above Google’s genuine browser. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description, but listed an entirely unrelated entity as its creator. Following widespread user complaints online, Google moved quickly to take down the fake listing.The issue came to light on October 14 after a Reddit user posted a screenshot showing two nearly identical Chrome apps appearing side-by-side in Google Play search results. The top result – promoted via a paid sponsored slot – featured the official Chrome name and logo, but displayed Hizbartech as the publisher. The legitimate Google Chrome app, published by Google LLC, appeared underneath the imposter ad.The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy, so everyday users looking for the browser could easily be fooled.Reported investigations show that the fake app did not start life as a browser clone.The app first appeared on the Play Store in August 2026 as a mobile game named Ball Bounce. But in late September 2026, the developer altered the existing listing, changing the title, graphics and descriptions to impersonate Google Chrome. The application kept the original base Android package name of com.ballbounce.Hizbartech.This repurposing explains the high download metric: the 1 lakh (100,000) installs reflected historical downloads accumulated while the app operated as a casual game, rather than 100,000 users intentionally installing a cloned browser.Users who downloaded the app reported that it did not function as a web browser at all. Instead, it opened into an unrelated chat utility featuring digital avatars and automated replies.The clearest indicator that the app was a fake was the developer profile. Google’s official browser is published by Google LLC, not third-party accounts like Hizbartech. “Key verification checks” are the key to prevent malicious downloads on Android:Android users who mistakenly download the counterfeit Chrome app – or anyone who still has the original Ball Bounce app by Hizbartech installed – should delete the application from your device immediately. Run Google Play Protect. Open the Google Play Store, navigate to Play Protect, and run an immediate device scan to detect any lingering malicious files.
Article Summary: A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description. The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ‘strongly’ disagrees with OpenAI’s Sam Altman on AI agents hacking websites, ‘I’m willing to accept no…’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Sam Altman’s acceptable tradeoffs vs. Jensen Huang’s absolute containment

OpenAI’s AI agents hack Hugging Face

Jensen Huang dismisses existential AI doomerism

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has drawn a sharp line against cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, insisting the tech sector should have zero tolerance for such breaches. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.“I’m willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them.We should do everything we can to avoid them,” Huang told Fortune in an interview in London.Huang’s remarks come after statements by Altman suggesting the public must tolerate a degree of digital fallout as AI advances. Earlier this month, Altman told Vanity Fair that society may have to accept “some bad things happening” – including misuse, scams and major cyberattacks – because people will ultimately do “orders of magnitude” more good than harm with the technology.Shortly after, during an appearance on Politico’s Decoded podcast, Altman warned of “a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems” originating from rival open-source systems.A few months ago, a swarm of OpenAI's own experimental agents broke out of their training sandbox and breached the Hugging Face platform. Huang flatly rejected the idea that these incidents are the price of progress, arguing that every breach reported so far could have been prevented with stricter oversight and better sandboxing.Comparing the challenge to the early days of the consumer internet, Huang noted that early web browsers initially allowed malicious websites to infect host computers with viruses. The solution was sandboxing: forcing browsers to run websites in isolated containers so they could never access or alter the underlying operating system.According to Huang, autonomous AI agents require the exact same architectural isolation, which is sealed inside secure digital containers to ensure they cannot touch, compromise, or damage anything beyond their strictly authorised operational boundaries.Beyond immediate cybersecurity debates, the Nvidia chief dismissed broader warnings of existential catastrophe voiced by executives across leading labs, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Maintaining that the software remains “completely in our control,” Huang questioned the logic of building systems if leaders genuinely believe they pose an extinction threat.“I don’t know why anybody would want to support the advancement of a technology that’s going to result, you know, in the end of human civilization as we know it. And so, if they believe that, they really ought to stop working on it,” Huang said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says tech sector should have zero tolerance for cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.

Article Title: Microsoft fixes 1,411 vulnerabilities in record October 2026 security update
Article Text:
Microsoft Windows 11

Breakdown by vulnerability type

Elevation of Privilege: 677 vulnerabilities

Remote Code Execution: 317 vulnerabilities

Information Disclosure: 254 vulnerabilities

Denial of Service: 73 vulnerabilities

Security Feature Bypass: 40 vulnerabilities

Spoofing: 28 vulnerabilities

Microsoft security patch: Three zero-days addressed

End of support deadlines for Windows 11 and Windows 10

Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day and two publicly disclosed zero-day flaws. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs across its software ecosystem. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.The tally counts only updates released directly on Patch this week itself, excluding 348 separate flaws resolved earlier this month across Azure API Center, Azure App Service, Azure Event Grid, Azure SRE Agent, Mariner, Microsoft Bookings, Microsoft Dataverse, Microsoft Exchange Server and Microsoft Partner Center.Across the release, elevation of privilege and remote execution bugs made up the vast majority of the patched flaws:Microsoft defines a zero-day vulnerability as a flaw that has been publicly disclosed or actively exploited before an official patch exists. The October update resolves three such weaknesses. In one case, attackers actively exploited this flaw to evade Windows' “Mark of the Web” security mechanism.Microsoft warned that “improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network. ”The second local security bypass flaw was discovered by James Forshaw of Google Project Zero, and allows authenticated attackers to subvert Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) and launch unauthorized applications.Thirdly, the flaw is caused by improperly controlled sequential memory allocation within .NET, and enables unauthorised attackers to trigger a denial-of-service condition over a network. Microsoft did not disclose who reported the vulnerability.Alongside the security updates, Microsoft formally marked end-of-support milestones for multiple operating system editions:“Today, October 13, 2026, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 have reached end of updates. The October 2026 monthly security update is the last update available for these editions,” Microsoft stated.
Article Summary: Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.

Article Title: Government issues critical warning as AI agents access Indian companies' confidential data
Article Text:
Representative image

CERT-In shares two incidents of AI models accessing company data without authorisation

AI tools cut cyberattack timelines from days to hours

CERT-In's advice to companies and AI developers

India’s cybersecurity agency, CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning artificial intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of companies without authorisation. In its advisory titled ‘AI Agents as Attack Vectors’, the cyber agency said that threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks. It highlighted two distinct categories of incidents targeting the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure of Indian entities.In one case, AI agents accessed business records containing personal and confidential information. In another, cybercriminals used AI-powered tools to find security gaps and launch financially motivated attacks against Indian organisations.During these incidents, the AI agents accessed business records containing personal data and confidential information. They used credentials and connection settings that had been left exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and cloud service roles with excessive permissions, the agency said.Notably, none of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access themselves, PTI reported.According to CERT-In, the use of AI agents has sharply reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage. In the campaign it identified, the gap shrank from several days to a few hours.Organisations that only partly fixed the security weaknesses were attacked again within days, with the attacks carried out on a larger scale, the agency said. CERT-In noted that basic security failures were behind all the recent AI agent-driven incidents it observed. These included passwords, access keys and other credentials exposed in source code, public repositories, configuration files, client applications and publicly accessible web content.Other weaknesses included old or test application programming interfaces (APIs) that remained accessible over the internet, payment API keys stored in plain text, cloud systems with excessive permissions, and management interfaces exposed to the internet.Unpatched software, weak passwords and a lack of multi-factor authentication also left systems vulnerable. AI agents were able to find and exploit these gaps faster and on a larger scale than human attackers.To reduce these risks, CERT-In has asked organisations to check their source code, public repositories and their commit histories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials. The agency has recommended that companies change exposed credentials and remove them from code histories. They should also shut down unused, outdated and test APIs, limit cloud access to only what is required, take administrative interfaces off the public internet and enforce multi-factor authentication.Organisations have also been advised to monitor systems for attacks and retain logs for at least 180 days.CERT-In said companies should treat their systems as compromised after a credential leak or confirmed intrusion until a forensic investigation clears them. They should also prepare for repeat attack attempts within days or weeks.For AI developers, research laboratories and evaluation agencies, the agency recommended isolating research and testing environments. Outbound network access should be blocked except where a task specifically requires it, with restrictions enforced at the network level rather than through instructions given to the AI model.It also advised using synthetic targets and test credentials instead of real production data during research and evaluation.
Article Summary: India’s cybersecurity agency, CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning artificial intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of companies without authorisation. The agency said that threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks.

Article Title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra named one of TIME’s Best Inventions for 2026
Article Text:
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has been named to TIME’s annual list of Best Inventions 2026, marking the fourth year a Samsung Galaxy device has earned a place on the prestigious list. The Galaxy S26 Ultra offers the most advanced Galaxy S series experience to date with a powerful camera system, premium performance, and intuitive Galaxy AI. The smartphone features the world’s first built-in Privacy Display for mobile phones, Super Steady video with horizontal lock, and tools for creating pro-grade content.With intuitive Galaxy AI working proactively and seamlessly on users’ behalf, Galaxy S26 Ultra is designed to help people focus on what they want to accomplish rather than how the technology works. The world’s first built-in Privacy Display for mobile phones is another highlight of the phone.“Together, these advancements reflect Samsung’s vision for technology that fades into the background while usefulness comes to the foreground, making innovation something people can depend on every day,” the company said.Beside Galaxy S26 Ultra, two other Samsung products also made this year’s list: the Bespoke AI Family Hub Refrigerator with AI Vision and the Odyssey G8 Gaming Monitor (G80HS).The Bespoke AI Family Hub Refrigerator with AI Vision offers advanced AI-powered food management, a personalized kitchen experience and hands-free convenience.This year’s major software update upgraded the refrigerator’s AI Vision technology, enabling it to recognize and track a wider range of fresh and processed foods to make meal planning and grocery shopping easier. With enhanced Now Brief and Voice ID features, it delivers personalized calendars, reminders, and recipes, while Auto Open & Close Doors allow users to open and close the refrigerator with a light touch or simple voice command.The 32-inch Samsung Odyssey G8 Gaming Monitor (G80HS), on the other hand, sets an industry milestone as the industry’s first 6K gaming monitor, marking a significant leap beyond 4K gaming standards. 6K resolution presents exceptional visual clarity and detail, enhancing immersion while providing a larger screen for both gaming and multitasking. Featuring 224PPI and an IPS panel, the monitor ensures sharp detail and visual fidelity across every frame and it delivers ultra-high 6K resolution at up to 165Hz, while Dual Mode enables up to 330Hz at 3K resolution.
Article Summary: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has been named to TIME’s annual list of Best Inventions 2026. This is the fourth year a Samsung Galaxy device has earned a place on the prestigious list. The smartphone features the first built-in Privacy Display for mobile phones.
